name: cv-baseline
hypothesis: Reference point: main's default config — linear probe on frozen YAMNet, Dropout(0.2), BinaryCrossentropy(label_smoothing=0.2), Adam 0.002 — under the general translation.
conclusion: The baseline every CV-era experiment compares against. Model kept at models/yamnet_medium_general.

name: binary-translation-cv
hypothesis: Collapsing every non-buzz label into one 'nonbuzz' class focuses the probe on the buzz boundary, instead of spending capacity on auxiliary classes.
conclusion: Neutral on the endpoint (-0.003), but binary's scores are far less portable across deployments: under one global threshold it looks much better (0.315 vs 0.262 pooled) because its score scale is consistent, not because it detects more. This pair is why the endpoint is per-deployment. Model kept at models/yamnet_medium_binary. Matches the pre-CV 'binary-translation' finding that multi-class auxiliary supervision is worth keeping.

name: context-stack
hypothesis: Buzz is sustained and the hard negatives are transient; stacking each frame's embedding with t-1 and t+1 gives the probe the duration cue it currently throws away.
conclusion: Positive, +0.050; 8/11 folds up, 6/8 among folds with >=3000 val frames. Cheapest structural win so far — no re-extraction. Not shippable until stack_context is mirrored in the inference wrapper (model.py feeds 1024-dim to a 3072-dim model). Eval is optimistic: snip frames all share a label so neighbours always agree, unlike continuous audio. Next: mirror in inference, sweep k=2,3, investigate the willard regression.

name: yamnet-combined
hypothesis: YAMNet's 521 AudioSet class scores are a nonlinear read of the same audio that a linear probe cannot construct for itself; concatenating them with the 1024-d embedding (1545-d) should add usable signal.
conclusion: Positive but modest, +0.016; 7/11 folds up, 6/8 among folds with >=3000 val frames and both declines there under 0.01. The two biggest movers (+0.180 at 2025-08-27/48, -0.153 at 2025-08-05/31) are both small folds and cancel; the latter early-stopped at epoch 6 and looks like a bad draw. Needed no code changes, but costs a re-extraction. The sigmoid scores are ~10x smaller than the embedding activations and nothing normalizes inputs - try standardizing the two blocks before judging the ceiling. Try before composing with context-stack.

name: context-embedder
hypothesis: exp/context-stack's +0.050 was measured on cached embeddings bucketed by label, so every frame's neighbours shared its own label - an artifact continuous audio can't reproduce, and the stacking lived in training code so the shipped model can't run it. Moving the same stack(t-1,t,t+1) into a new embedder, fed real neighbouring audio from the snip, should ship and measure honestly.
conclusion: Positive, +0.022; 7/11 folds up including the two largest movers (+0.140, +0.102), 4 down but only one (1_23, 315 val frames) is small enough to discount. Ships: model.py sizes its input layer from n_embeddings (3072) automatically and inference calls the same embed(). As predicted, well below context-stack's optimistic 0.256 - the gap is roughly the size of the same-label-neighbour artifact. willard (recorders/willard/2024-08-07/1_11) loses here too (-0.059), same fold context-stack lost on (-0.074), so that regression is a property of the deployment, not the cached-eval bug; worth the willard-regression listening pass next.

name: input-standardization
hypothesis: exp/yamnet-combined's +0.016 concatenated two feature blocks on very different scales (score block ~10x smaller than the embedding block) with nothing normalizing the input; a fixed Normalization layer, adapt()-ed on training folds only, should let the probe use the score block properly and shows whether the gain is a ceiling or an artifact of the scores being drowned out.
conclusion: Flat headline vs yamnet-combined (-0.004, 0.222->0.218; +0.012 vs cv-baseline), but carried entirely by one small/unreliable fold (2025-08-27/48, -0.156, 1570 val frames) that swung just as hard the other way when yamnet-combined was first measured. On the 8 folds with >=3000 val frames, standardization adds +0.014 on top of yamnet-combined (6/8 up) - the scale-mismatch hypothesis was real. Caveat: 10/11 folds ran the full 400-epoch cap under standardization vs a median ~120 for the unstandardized baseline, and best_val_loss came in higher despite sens improving in most folds - the fixed LR/patience were tuned for the old input scale and were never revisited. Not adopted on this evidence; see IDEAS.md's standardization-convergence for the LR/patience resweep this leaves open. No model shipped.

name: class-weight-fix
hypothesis: class_weight= passed to model.fit() is invalid for this model's multi-hot multi-label targets: Keras collapses y via argmax(y, axis=-1) to one scalar per sample, picked by class-index order (alphabetical), and applies it to the whole sample's loss rather than per-neuron. Any frame where ins_buzz co-occurs with an earlier-sorted class (ambient_*/animal/human) never gets ins_buzz's weight applied at all - verified against Keras 3.14.1 source and directly against the medium set (342/5478 pickles hit this). Replacing class_weight= with a custom loss (tf.nn.weighted_cross_entropy_with_logits, pos_weight per class) applies the same balanced weight table correctly per-neuron, reweighting only the positive term and leaving negative supervision untouched.
conclusion: Positive but modest, +0.013; 7/11 folds up. The two biggest movers each direction (+0.114 at 2025-08-12/1_114, +0.086 at 2025-08-05/31 up; -0.056 at JamesU, -0.038 at wooster down) are all folds with enough val frames (>3700) to trust individually, so this is a genuine majority-positive result, not a landslide masked by noise. The underlying bug is real and affected every CV-era log entry including cv-baseline itself (same weighting bug present in all of them), but the size of this correction is comparable to several logged wins rather than a wholesale invalidation - re-baselining the log is a judgment call for whoever reads this next, not decided here.

name: yamnet-native-buzz
hypothesis: YAMNet's own AudioSet-trained classification head might score insect buzzing better than our probe, since AudioSet is far larger than our field-recording set even if less task-specific. No training: take the frozen weight column + bias for AudioSet class 125 ('Buzz') off YAMNet's original Dense(521) layer and score it directly on our existing embeddings.
conclusion: Decisive negative. 9/11 folds scored, all near zero (0.000-0.034) including every large fold (4700-6900 val frames each) - not a small-fold artifact. Pooled ROC shows some separation (sens~0.30 at fpr~0.40) so the neuron isn't dead, just nowhere near usable at operating FPR. AudioSet's 'Buzz' class likely covers buzzers/electric buzz broadly rather than insect wingbeat specifically, and clip-level 521-way training doesn't sharpen a frame-level insect boundary. 'Bee, wasp, etc.' (class 126) and 'Insect' (class 121, the most literal match) tried too, same result (0.002 and 0.005, all folds near zero) - not a wrong-class-pick issue. 'Cricket', 'Mosquito', 'Fly, housefly' untested, but three classes landing in the same place rules out class choice as the explanation; off-the-shelf YAMNet classification is not worth pursuing further here.

name: tail-loss
hypothesis: An OHEM-style hard-negative-mining term added to BCE(label_smoothing=0.2), targeting the top fraction of highest-scoring ins_buzz negatives per training batch, should specifically lift sensitivity at the low-FPR operating point rather than reshaping the whole score distribution the way focal loss does.

baseline.note: same 2 folds as this entry; cv-baseline's 11-fold figure is 0.206 and is NOT what this row compares against

conclusion: NOT A FAIR TEST OF THE HYPOTHESIS - stopped at 2 folds after finding an implementation flaw. Sensitivity over those 2 folds collapsed 0.305 -> 0.007 (ohem_frac=0.01, ohem_weight=1.0). Root cause is a monitor interaction, not a representational one: the OHEM term is part of the compiled loss, so Keras also evaluates it on the validation fold, where it feeds EarlyStopping's val_loss monitor. The term's hard-negative set is batch-local, and the validation batch (one fold, ~4-7k frames) is far smaller and noisier than the pooled training batch (~10 folds, ~65-70k frames), so val_loss hits a spurious minimum in the first few epochs and restore_best_weights locks in a near-random snapshot (best_epoch 6 and 17, vs baseline's 129 and 63 on the same folds). Reproduced on 2 large folds (6908 and 3768 val frames); ohem_weight=0.1 showed the same rising-val_loss shape before crashing on an unrelated TF graph bug (out-of-range gather under fused multi-step execution with a data-dependent top_k count). GENERAL LESSON FOR ANY CUSTOM LOSS: whatever you compile is what EarlyStopping monitors - a loss term whose value depends on within-batch rank is not a valid stopping signal on a single small validation fold. See IDEAS.md 'tail-loss-fair-retest' for the version worth running.

name: std-convergence
hypothesis: exp/input-standardization's Normalization layer left 10/11 folds running the full 400-epoch cap under the fixed lr=0.002/patience=50/min_delta=0.002 rule tuned for unstandardized inputs; a small LR/patience sweep on the fixed structure should find a setting under which it actually converges, giving an honest read of that structure's sens number.

metrics.note: NO full CV was run - 2-fold diagnostic only, no new sensitivity_mean produced. input-standardization's 0.218 still stands as the number for that structure.

conclusion: The sweep this idea called for was run on 2 large folds (lr in {5e-4,1e-3,2e-3}, +/- clipnorm=1.0) and came back negative-to-inconclusive. Lower LR does make early stopping fire (epoch ~60-95 vs the original's 397-400), but always at a WORSE best_val_loss and worse-or-equal sens than the original run that never stops - consistent with full-batch Adam still making real slow progress rather than failing to recognize a plateau. clipnorm=1.0 at the original LR neither induces earlier stopping nor helps. THREE FINDINGS BEYOND THE EXPERIMENT, all of general interest: (1) SEED NOISE - a same-config rerun (lr=2e-3, same fold) landed on a substantially different, worse trajectory purely from uncontrolled random init (early stop at epoch 127 vs the 400 cap; val_loss 0.633 vs 0.457). That is comparable in size to every LR effect tested here AND to several logged wins (+0.013 to +0.022). There is no seed control anywhere in the pipeline. (2) TRAINING IS FULL-BATCH - the batch size exceeds any fold's frame count, so one epoch is one gradient step, and the 400-epoch cap is 400 gradient steps. (3) NORMALIZATION IS NaN-PRONE on yamnet_combined - 52 of 1545 input dims have ~zero training variance, so the layer divides by sqrt(var+1e-7)~3e-4 and amplifies them ~3000x; a genuine NaN blowup occurred at lr=5e-4 without clipping. Structural, independent of LR. Standardized yamnet_combined not adopted; input-standardization's +0.014-on-reliable-folds is neither confirmed nor refuted, now for a documented reason rather than an open question.

name: context-pooling
hypothesis: A learned attention pool (softmax-weighted sum over stacked context frames) can reduce the yamnet_context embedder's (n_frames,1024) input to one 1024-d vector better than the flat linear probe used for the honest context-embedder result (+0.022), by letting the model weight the most informative frame rather than treating all 3072 dims equally.
conclusion: sens_persite 0.206 (cv-baseline) / 0.228 (context-embedder, the correct comparator for a pooling change) -> 0.049 (-0.157 / -0.179). 8-10/11 folds down under either comparator; the 1-2 nominal upticks are within noise on low-frames_val folds. Diagnosis: 6/11 folds went NaN in val_loss within epochs 1-4 (history.pickle), not min_delta early-stopping -- restore_best_weights kept a near-random pre-collapse checkpoint for those folds, which is why folds_summary.csv shows best_epoch 1-4 there. The other 5 folds trained normally (53-132 epochs) but still averaged sens 0.073, well below both comparators, so the pooling head underperforms even when training succeeds -- this isn't purely a stopped-too-early artifact. Attention pooling as implemented (Dense(1) score + softmax + Adam 0.002 + BCE label_smoothing=0.2) is numerically unstable on this embedder/loss combination and the direction is negative even ignoring the instability; treat as a dead structural idea for this pooling formulation, not just a bad run. A max-pool control (POOL_MODE='max') or lower LR is worth a quick check before concluding attention pooling per se cannot work, but no strong signal justifies more compute here.

name: context-width
hypothesis: k=2 temporal context ([t-2..t+2], 5 frames, 5120-d), dose-response step past context-embedder's k=1 (+0.022 clean); predicted willard regresses more than k=1's -0.059, sustained-buzz folds gain more.
conclusion: Reverses k=1's gain rather than extending it: sensitivity_mean 0.206 (baseline) -> 0.228 (k=1) -> 0.185 (k=2). vs k=1: 6/11 folds down, 4 up, 1 flat. Willard prediction held (regression roughly doubled, -0.059 -> -0.111 vs baseline, monotonic, early-stopped model consistent with dilution story). Sustained-buzz prediction only weakly supported (the one qualifying fold moves the predicted direction but by a negligible amount on a too-thin fold). Caveated: much of the magnitude rests on two volatile folds, one with best_epoch=1 (apparently undertrained) and one with 315 val frames; a same-day concurrent finding (tail-loss-retest) shows this set's per-fold sensitivity can swing 0.3+ from seed noise alone with no code change, so the turnover's direction is more trustworthy than its size.

name: framehop-overlap
hypothesis: Halving framehop_prop (1 -> 0.5, 50% overlap) roughly doubles frame density and should give short buzz events (willard: 68% <1s) a better-centred frame, improving sensitivity, willard especially.
conclusion: sensitivity_mean dropped 0.206->0.054 (-0.152), 10/11 folds down; willard collapsed with the cohort (0.177->0.003) rather than improving. Not trusted at face value: (1) halving hop ~doubled buzz_frames_total (5641->11225) and neg_frames_fold_median (22->43) uniformly (~2.0x every fold) -- sensitivity is a per-frame rate and denser overlap adds partial/edge-of-event frames that dilute it even at equal per-event detection; no event-level re-read was recoverable from predictions.csv (no event id/timestamp, only activation+correct per frame). (2) best_epoch collapsed (median 13 vs baseline 56; shipped epochs_fixed 13 vs 56, same batch size, ~2x frames/epoch so total frame-exposure at stop ~46% of baseline) -- EarlyStopping's fixed min_delta=0.002 looks miscalibrated for the new frames/epoch scale, and the same best_epoch collapse showed up in unrelated same-day experiments (context-width, attention pooling), suggesting a systemic stopping-rule issue rather than a hop-specific effect. Per-fold epoch-ratio only weakly correlates with per-fold delta (r=0.155), so the decline reads as broad/uniform rather than concentrated in the shortest-stopped folds. Read as inconclusive on the underlying hypothesis, not evidence overlapping hop hurts.

name: tail-loss-retest
hypothesis: exp/tail-loss's OHEM-on-hard-negatives term collapsed sensitivity for an implementation reason (EarlyStopping monitored the tail-contaminated compiled loss, plus a data-dependent top_k graph bug); fixing both (separate val_bce monitor, fixed-size ohem_k) should let the mechanism be tested honestly.

metrics.note: NO full CV was run - single-fold diagnostic only, per the brief's gate (best_epoch in baseline's ~60-130 ballpark, non-pathological sensitivity) before spending a CV.

conclusion: Both prescribed fixes ARE correctly implemented (confirmed EarlyStopping monitors val_bce not val_loss, confirmed via history.pickle that best_epoch tracks val_bce's minimum). Despite that, ohem_weight=1.0 still collapsed sensitivity to ~0.000 on fold 'JamesU - MustardBumbler/1_29' (baseline: best_epoch 63/113, sens 0.448) via genuine score inversion -- the fold's 30 highest-scoring frames were all negatives, positives ranked below the entire negative tail -- not a stopping-rule artifact. But a weight=0.0 control (mathematically identical to cv-baseline's loss), run through the same standalone single-fold harness, ALSO failed to reproduce baseline's number for this fold (best_epoch 9-47, sens 0.002-0.07 across 3 reruns), even when run through main's completely unmodified train.py on a throwaway script. This means the single-fold pre-check harness itself (introduced by exp/tail-loss, continued here) is not a reliable proxy for a CV fold's outcome in this pipeline -- consistent with exp/std-convergence's logged seed-noise finding but larger in magnitude, enough to fail the gate even for the null model. A directional signal survives that noise floor though: weight=1.0 was reproducibly worse (sensitivity 0.000, full score inversion) than every weight=0 control (0.002-0.07, no such inversion observed) on the same fold. Given the gate failed for both the config and its own control, and the directional evidence that the live OHEM gradient term still actively harms beyond the noise floor, no full CV was run -- spending an 11-fold CV on a mechanism already showing active harm at the single-fold level isn't where compute should go per LOOP.md. Flagging trust=artifact because the single-fold harness's inability to reproduce the null case makes any number from it (including the qualitative 0.000) partly a property of the measurement method, not just the mechanism. See notes.md on exp/tail-loss-retest for the full diagnostic trail, including a proposed new IDEAS.md line about the harness's reliability limits.

name: aug-snr-noise
hypothesis: Augmentation has always hurt because _apply_noise adds fixed-amplitude noise (RMS 0.029-0.115) landing 13-25 dB ABOVE the median buzz frame (RMS 0.006), making augmented positives broadband-noise-labeled-buzz. Scale noise per-frame to SNR 15 dB below signal instead.
conclusion: Inconclusive on endpoint (-0.007, folds 5/5/1) but a real departure from 'augmentation always hurts': SNR-15 noise is ~neutral where fixed-amplitude noise was clearly harmful. Residual drop carried by willard (-0.145, early-stopped epoch 10 vs 69) + 3 folds that early-stopped 3-6x sooner than baseline - the stopping-rule-scale confound (augmented copy ~doubles frames/epoch, fixed min_delta fires early); normally-trained folds net positive. Baseline re-trained on this machine/current set = 0.199 (logged cv-baseline 0.206 was an older fold roster). Also fixed augment.py stale --fold train default via --all-folds. See notes.md exp/aug-snr-noise.

name: aug-combine-overlap
hypothesis: CombineSpec mixup (buzz waveform-mixed with ambient_* background, re-embedded, labeled buzz) synthesizes buzz-over-novel-background examples; should lift held-out-deployment sens@fpr0.005, most on quiet-background folds. Scripts existed but were unusable: exact raw-label matching missed all ins_buzz_* ; --fold train default is pre-CV; empty pool raised.
conclusion: Neutral (+0.002, folds 4/5/2, all deltas small, best_epochs healthy 79-140 so no stopping confound - a cleaner null than aug-snr-noise). Combine/overlap aug of buzz over ambient neither helps nor hurts as configured. Caveat: mixing is WITHIN a recording (buzz+ambient from the same fold), the opposite of the 'different site's background' hypothesis; only 52/322 folds had both classes so 14780 frames added (~2.6x raw buzz on covered folds; all 11 rotate folds' buzz did get augmented into other pools). Also relaxed dataset.load_augmented to tolerate folds with no augment dir (required for any label-selective aug). Follow-up: cross-fold pairing draws augment frames from the whole pool. See notes.md exp/aug-combine-overlap.

name: embed-mixup
hypothesis: Embedding-space (manifold) mixup on frozen YAMNet embeddings, alpha=0.2, within the training pool only (both parents from train folds, val fold never enters _to_tf) — the one augmentation with a plausible mechanism for a frozen-embedding probe per the transfer-learning literature; expect small, most folds nudging same way.
conclusion: Leaning negative (-0.007 mean, 6/4/1 down/up/flat); the trustworthy high-buzz folds (JamesU -0.024 @6984 val frames, willard -0.040) are among the down-movers, the one real gain is a near-zero-buzz fold. Embedding-space mixup doesn't rescue augmentation for the frozen-YAMNet-probe setup. Frames/epoch unchanged so no stopping-rule-scale confound. Research: aug gains in the literature are at feature-extractor training time; a low-capacity probe over a frozen general embedder has little frame-level nuisance variance to regularise. notes.md exp/embed-mixup. Single run, no seed control.

name: trunk-frozen
hypothesis: Control for the trunk fine-tune runs: yamnet_trunk embedder (caches YAMNet layer-12 output; head rebuilds layers 13-14 + GAP from the real weights) with the backbone frozen is numerically the stock linear probe (verified 1.06e-3 max diff vs the yamnet embedding), but must run at --batch 1024 / --lr-head 2e-4 (12288-d cannot fit a bigger batch in 2.4GB VRAM), so it is not cv-baseline. Measures what that regime change alone costs.
conclusion: +0.017 vs cv-baseline; per fold the two track closely (|delta|<0.02 on 6/11), trunk_frozen up on ~7/11. Batch 1024 + lr 2e-4 vs full-batch + lr 2e-3 plus the float16 trunk cache -- within std-convergence's 0.013-0.022 same-config rerun noise. Exists as the paired comparator for exp/trunk-ft-1e5 and -5e5 so their deltas are not confounded with this regime change. notes.md on exp/trunk-ft.

name: trunk-ft-1e5
hypothesis: Unfreeze YAMNet's last two blocks (layers 13-14, ~1.6M params) at a differential rate -- backbone 1e-5, head 2e-4 -- via yamnet_trunk + an AdamMultiLR per-variable LR scale. yamnet-ft tried this pre-rework (13-14 at 1e-5) and lost 8.3pp on the retired corpus/fixed split; temporal-context already showed such a verdict inverting under CV.
conclusion: +0.046 vs the matched frozen control (9/11 folds up, 2 down both <0.011; mean per-fold delta +0.046), +0.063 vs cv-baseline (10/11 up). Largest structural gain in the CV log; inverts yamnet-ft. val_loss also lower for ft on nearly every fold. Big movers include willard (the fold temporal context regressed on, willard-regression in IDEAS) and Opp/2025-08-12. Direction is clean (most folds same way, several >0.05); size is caveated -- several folds restore very early epochs (best 2/5/9/10: small-batch noisy val_loss, stopping-rule-scale), though the frozen control shares that regime so the paired delta absorbs most of it; and trunk_frozen itself is +0.017 over cv-baseline. No seed control. Follow-ups: LR/patience sweep tuned for batch 1024, then augmentation, then unfreeze more/fewer blocks. notes.md on exp/trunk-ft.

name: trunk-ft-5e5
hypothesis: Same as trunk-ft-1e5 but backbone LR 5e-5 (5x faster) -- does a less gentle backbone rate help or tip into overfit?
conclusion: +0.041 vs frozen (9/11 up, 2 down), effectively tied with trunk-ft-1e5 (+0.046). The unfreezing gain is robust to backbone LR across 1e-5..5e-5. best_epoch restores are even earlier here (4,1,6,11 on several folds) -- 5e-5 overfits slightly more -- so 1e-5 is the pick. Same caveats as trunk-ft-1e5. notes.md on exp/trunk-ft.

name: trunk-ft-1e5-aug
hypothesis: Within-fold additive-noise augmentation (NoiseSpec prop=0.05, generated through yamnet_trunk for all 11 rotate folds) on top of trunk-ft-1e5. Waveform aug is ~neutral on a frozen probe (aug gains are at encoder-train time per the literature); now that the backbone is being trained, aug might finally help.

baseline.note: compare paired on the 5 completed folds only, not these scalars

conclusion: NEGATIVE, stopped at 5/11 (direction was clear and each fold is ~2x slower with the doubled pool). Paired vs trunk-ft-1e5 on the 5 folds: 4 down 1 up, mean delta -0.060; willard collapses -0.210 with best_epoch 1, Diel/2026-04-08 best_epoch 1 too -- the additive noise spikes val_loss immediately and restore_best_weights locks a near-random snapshot (same monitor failure mode as tail-loss, and load_augmented feeds aug to training only but the distribution shift still wrecks the val_loss curve shape). Unfreezing the backbone did NOT turn waveform aug into a win. Consistent with LOOP.md's standing 'augmentation has hurt'. If revisited: much smaller prop, and keep aug out of the early-stopping monitor. notes.md on exp/trunk-ft.

name: trunk-ft-stop-sweep
hypothesis: trunk-ft-1e5's early best_epoch restores (2,5,9,10 on several folds) suggested EarlyStopping min_delta=0.002 on val_loss is mis-scaled for batch 1024 and stops short of the val_loss minimum, leaving sensitivity on the table. Sweep min_delta (0.002 -> 1e-4 -> 0) and patience (50 -> 100) on 3 diagnostic folds, then a full CV at the best setting.

metrics.note: 3-fold diagnostic + 3/11 of a full CV at min_delta 1e-4; no full sensitivity_mean produced

conclusion: NON-LEVER. A fresh run of the IDENTICAL trunk-ft-1e5 config moved the 3-fold mean +0.018 and best_epoch by 15-50 epochs (27/46/3 vs the original 9/94/2) -- pure run-to-run noise, no seed control (std-convergence redux). min_delta 0.002 -> 1e-4 moved the same 3-fold mean +0.015, i.e. within that noise. Partial full CV at min_delta 1e-4 (stopped 3/11, each fold runs 2-3x longer -- willard took 225 epochs): +0.015/+0.032/-0.020 vs trunk-ft-1e5, folds split. trunk-ft-1e5's early best_epochs were val_loss-trajectory noise, not a systematic stopping failure; the sens@best-vs-peak gaps are the sens@fpr monitor's own noise (~20 neg frames/fold). Keep trunk-ft-1e5's config (min_delta 0.002, patience 50). Added --min-delta and --only-folds (diagnostic fold filter) to 03_train. The prerequisite for any real tuning here is noise-floor-cv. notes.md on exp/trunk-ft.

name: noise-floor-cv
hypothesis: Repeat cv-baseline's exact config as a fresh full CV to quantify run-to-run noise (no seed control anywhere); the denominator every per-fold delta in the log is read against.
conclusion: Noise floor: median per-fold |delta| ~0.017, headline mean -0.014 (6up/4down/1flat, same config/data), quiet folds swing 0.03-0.13. Sub-0.015 split-fold deltas in the log (binary, embed-mixup, class-weight, aug-*, trunk-ft min_delta sweep) are inside this floor. trunk-ft-1e5's +0.046 at 9/11 one-way clears it on direction but willard alone (+0.114 that run vs -0.089 from noise here) inflates the size to ~+0.039 over the other 10. One repeat = a floor, not a variance estimate.
